findings.description: The 'Crate naming convention' section classifies crate families (sc-jev-*, sc-decision-*) and reserves crate names (sc-decider*, sc-laya*, sc-kev*). That is a structural decision (crate taxonomy). It is recorded only in an unnumbered architecture section and in plan.md owner item 12 (plan.md:663-668). No ADR records it. ADR-SAG-0030's per-API bullet (architecture.md:1611-1615) covers modules only, not crate names.
findings.remediation: Record the crate-family rule and the reserved sc-decider*/sc-laya*/sc-kev* names in an ADR (new Proposed ADR, or an ADR-SAG-0030 amendment that names the amended ADR), or remove the naming reservation from this record. No new gate is needed.

findings.description: The naming rule says sc-jev-* is 'anything that speaks the TypeSafe Jev API, including Haiku and Luna'. This contradicts ADR-SAG-0007 (Haiku/Luna use provider HTTP only, docs/architecture.md:666-667), ADR-SAG-0012 (Jev HTTP lives only in sc-jev, lines 1016-1017), ADR-SAG-0019 (Haiku/Luna body is not Jev's body, lines 431-434), the roadmap row that calls Haiku/Luna 'API-direct Anthropic / OpenAI' (architecture.md:1135), and docs/sc-jev-backends/architecture.md:18 ('not the Jev wire document'). The 'Today' list also omits sc-jev-py (crates/sc-jev-py exists) and includes sc-jev-check and sc-jev-host, which do not speak the Jev API. The same wording is in plan.md:663-665.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the sc-jev-* sentence to: sc-jev-* holds the crates that send TypeSafe Jev API requests (sc-jev, sc-jev-check, sc-jev-host, sc-jev-py as facade and composition). sc-jev-backends keeps its historical name and is the provider-HTTP (LLM) crate under ADR-SAG-0007. Correct the 'Today' list to include sc-jev-py. Apply the same edit to plan.md item 12. Do not rename crates and do not add a gate.

findings.description: Three sources disagree on when jev::v1 is built. The r-7 Layering note says 'only jev:: is built in r-7' (lines 202-203). The r-7 outcome says jev::v1 is r-5's (line 196), owned_paths exclude src/jev/** and tests/jev.rs as r-5 (line 83), and the manifest adds the jev root in r-5 (line 249). ADR-SAG-0030's per-API bullet says 'jev::v1 now' (architecture.md:1611-1612), while its Status line and 'Jev API structs' bullet put jev::v1 in r-5 (architecture.md:1559-1560, 1593). The 'API-agnostic' claim (architecture.md:1614, sprint-r-7:202) also sits uneasily with jev::v1 (Jev-specific) inside sc-decision-schema, and with architecture.md:58-59 ('sc-decision-* is the API-agnostic layer').
findings.remediation: Change the r-7 Layering note to 'jev:: is reserved here and built in r-5'. Change the ADR-SAG-0030 per-API bullet to 'jev::v1 lands in r-5 (see the Jev API structs bullet)'. State in the crate-naming text that sc-decision-schema is API-agnostic except for per-API modules (jev::v1 under ADR-SAG-0012 r-5). Keep the r-5 file ownership unchanged.

findings.description: The new 'Per-API modules' bullet is tagged '(Recorded; post-MVP)' and has no owning sprint, no '(Proposed, r-7)' marker and no owner-gate note. r-7 D9 flips only '(Proposed, r-7)' markers, so after the ADR becomes Active it is unclear whether this bullet is binding.
findings.remediation: State in the bullet whether it is binding ('Recorded; binding as a reservation, no module built before r-5/post-MVP') or non-binding. Name the owner or sprint that flips it, following the 'Scope context' precedent.
